title: The Wrong Question
content:
"Will AI replace me?" is the wrong question.

The right question is: "How do I become irreplaceable WITH AI?"

Here's what I've learned teaching 7 cohorts of creative professionals:

The people who thrive aren't hiding from AI.
They're not competing with AI.
They're building WITH AI.

Your domain expertise + AI literacy = an unbeatable combination.

The designers who understand their craft AND can build custom GPTs?
The writers who know story AND can create content workflows?
The photographers who have an eye AND can automate post-processing?

That's the future. And it's already here.

The question isn't whether AI changes your field.
It's whether you're driving that change or getting driven by it.

What side are you on?

#AIforCreatives #FutureOfWork #CreativeProfessionals

Web 2.0: "Social media will ruin attention spans and journalism."
It changed them. Some for worse. Some for better.

AI Era: "AI will replace creative professionals."
Sound familiar?

The pattern is always the same:
1. Initial panic
2. Early adopters experiment
3. Best practices emerge
4. Adaptation becomes normal
5. New opportunities appear

We're somewhere between 2 and 3 right now.

The creatives who figured out Web 1.0 early? They dominated.
The ones who mastered social? Same thing.

AI is no different.

The question isn't IF you'll adapt. It's WHEN.

#ThirdTripAroundTheSun #AIAdoption #CreativeEvolution

When I teach creative professionals about AI, ethics comes on Day 1. Not Day 6.

Why?

Because AI literacy isn't just about building tools.
It's about:
- Recognizing AI-generated content
- Understanding bias in training data
- Navigating copyright complexities
- Discerning deepfakes from reality

The Pope Francis jacket photo fooled millions.
AI-generated text is getting harder to detect.
Voice cloning is good enough to fool family members.

Critical evaluation isn't a nice-to-have.
It's the core skill of our era.

The creative professionals who thrive won't just USE AI.
They'll understand it well enough to detect it.

Are you ready?

#MediaLiteracy #AIEthics #CriticalThinking

Your worldview is:

- Hard-won lessons from failures no one else had

Voice is mimicable.
Worldview is not.

This is why I tell every creative professional:
Build assistants that know your voice AND your worldview.

The voice gets your tone right.
The worldview gets your thinking right.

That combination? That's your competitive moat.

AI without your worldview = generic output
AI with your worldview = YOUR amplified output

Don't just train AI on how you write.
Train it on how you think.

title: The POP Framework
content:
Every AI platform. One framework.

P - Persona: Who should AI act as?
O - Objective: What specific task should it accomplish?
P - Parameters: How should it deliver? (tone, length, format)

This works in ChatGPT. In Claude. In Gemini. In custom GPTs.

Why? Because these aren't platform-specific tricks.
They're principles of clear communication.

When you give AI:
- A clear role (Persona)
- A specific goal (Objective)
- Defined constraints (Parameters)

You get dramatically better outputs.

Example:
BAD: "Write me a blog post about AI"
GOOD: "You are a senior marketing strategist (P). Write a 800-word blog post about AI adoption for creative agencies (O). Use conversational tone, include 3 specific examples, and end with a clear call-to-action (P)."

Same AI. Same prompt box. Completely different results.

The POP Framework changed how I teach AI.
It'll change how you use it.

#POPFramework #PromptEngineering #AIFramework

title: Quality Over Quantity
content:
"About 15-20 substantial documents. You don't need hundreds. Quality over quantity."

That's my advice for knowledge bases.

I see people dump 500 documents into a custom GPT and wonder why it performs poorly.

More isn't better. Better is better.

Your knowledge base hierarchy:
1. Primary sources (original documents, transcripts)
2. Synthesized materials (summaries, analyses)
3. Reference materials (style guides, process docs)

15-20 high-quality documents > 500 random files.

Curate ruthlessly.
Include only what your AI actually needs to know.
Remove anything that could confuse or contradict.

The quality of your knowledge base determines the quality of your assistant.

That's not a slogan. It's physics.

#KnowledgeBase #AIQuality #Curation

title: The Agentic Spectrum
content:
Not every problem needs an agent.

Here's the Agentic Spectrum:

ASSISTANTS: Human-in-the-loop, conversational, real-time
- Best for: ideation, writing, analysis, creative work
- Example: Custom GPT for your client's brand voice

AUTOMATIONS: Trigger-based, workflow-oriented, background
- Best for: repetitive tasks, data processing, notifications
- Example: New transcript → AI summary → Slack notification

AGENTS: Autonomous, multi-step, tool-using
- Best for: complex research, multi-iteration tasks
- Example: Deep research across multiple sources

Most people jump to agents because they sound impressive.

But 80% of the time, a well-built assistant is enough.

Start simple. Add complexity only when needed.

The skill isn't using the fanciest tool.
The skill is choosing the right tool for the job.

#AgenticSpectrum #AITools #RightToolRightJob

title: It's Iterative
content:
"Multiple iterations. The first version was way too generic. I kept testing it, seeing where it went wrong, and tightening the instructions."

That's the honest truth about building AI assistants.

Your first version will be mediocre.
Your fifth version will be good.
Your tenth version will be great.

The process:
1. Build version 1 (expect it to be rough)
2. Test it with real prompts
3. Identify where it fails
4. Ask: Missing knowledge? Bad instructions? Wrong constraints?
5. Update accordingly
6. Test again
7. Repeat

This isn't a bug. This is the process.

Your assistant gets smarter as you learn what it needs.

Stop expecting perfection on attempt one.
Start expecting improvement on every attempt.

#IterativeProcess #AILearning #ContinuousImprovement

AI output can LOOK like real work without BEING real work.

The report looks professional... but says nothing actionable.
The website looks polished... but doesn't serve real users.

This is the "looks good" trap.

The solution isn't less AI.
The solution is better validation.

Get it in front of humans.
Test it with real users.
Validate before you publish.

AI accelerates production.
Humans validate quality.

Don't confuse a polished appearance with actual value.

If you can:
- Write clear instructions
- Curate relevant documents
- Make decisions about scope

You can build a custom GPT.

The barrier isn't technical.
The barrier is just getting started.

Stop building complexity for its own sake.

title: Credit-Saving Hack
content:
Lovable.dev hack that saves serious money:

Instead of submitting suggested prompts one by one:

1. Click first suggestion → it populates the input box
2. Copy it
3. Delete from input box
4. Click second suggestion
5. Paste the first one after
6. Repeat for 3rd, 4th, 5th
7. Submit ALL at once

Multiple improvements for the cost of one credit.

Another hack:
Refine your prompts in ChatGPT BEFORE putting them in Lovable.

ChatGPT is cheaper.
Get your prompt right there.
Then use your Lovable credits on generation.

Every credit you save = more iterations.
More iterations = better outcomes.

#VibeCodingHacks #SaveCredits #SmartIteration

title: Visual Edits
content:
Stop wasting credits on simple changes.

Lovable.dev has a "Visual Edits" mode most people miss.

Instead of writing "Change the button color to blue" (costs credit):

1. Click "Visual Edits" button
2. Click directly on the element
3. Change the property in the panel
4. Save

No credit used.

Use prompts for:
- Structural changes
- Adding new sections
- Rethinking layouts

Use visual edits for:
- Color changes
- Text updates
- Font adjustments
- Small positioning tweaks

Know when to prompt. Know when to edit directly.

That's efficiency.

#VisualEdits #VibeCodingEfficiency #SmartWorkflow
